title: Events
subtitle: Query and transaction events as a JSON stream.
intro: Forward DuckDB lifecycle events to an executable handler as JSON lines on standard input. Use the stream for operational logs, query timing and transaction traces, with a session tag to identify each running process.

reference.name: events_destination
reference.description: Absolute path to the executable that consumes JSON lines.

reference.name: events_types
reference.description: List of enabled query, connection or transaction event types.

reference.name: events_session_name
reference.description: Tag each event with a process or workload identifier.

reference.name: events_async
reference.description: TRUE enables asynchronous delivery; default is FALSE.

reference.name: query_id / transaction_id
reference.description: Correlate query pairs and the enclosing transaction.

reference.name: has_error / error_message
reference.description: Inspect failures on query_end and transaction_rollback events.

notes.title: A handler is required
notes.body: Create an executable with a shebang at the configured absolute path. It must read stdin line by line and persist or process each JSON object. The extension launches the handler with DuckDB's privileges.

notes.title: Lifecycle and availability
notes.body: Settings belong to the running process; reapply them at startup. Async delivery trades reliability for query latency. Persist events in the handler when durability matters. Community package availability varies by DuckDB version and platform.
